PSALM 35

. The Psalmist invokes God's aid, contrasting the hypocrisy, cunning, and malice of his enemies with his integrity and generosity. The imprecations of the first part including a brief notice of their conduct, the fuller exposition of their hypocrisy and malice in the second, and the earnest prayer for deliverance from their scornful triumph in the last, are each closed (, , , , ) with promises of praise for the desired relief, in which his friends will unite. The historical occasion is probably .

7-8. net in a pit--or, "pit of their net"--or, "net-pit," as "holy hill" for "hill of holiness" (); a figure from hunting (). spoiling--literally, "bereavement." The usual modes of showing grief are made, as figures, to express his sorrow.

abjects--either as cripples (compare ), contemptible; or, degraded persons, such as had been beaten (compare ).

tear me, and ceased not--literally, "were not silent"--showing that the tearing meant slandering.

wink with the eye--an insulting gesture ().

without a cause--manifests more malice than having a wrong cause.
